title: Dead-code duplicate suppressor still exists (detectors/honeypot_suppressor.py)
detail: Confirmed genuinely inert -- should_suppress() in this file is never called from anywhere in the codebase (real, active logic now lives in alert-engine/correlator.py, fixed separately). Safe to delete this file in a future cleanup pass, or leave as reference -- does not affect runtime behavior either way.

title: Agent stats dict shows 0/0/0/0 on some runs despite correct fflush() and min_uid filtering
detail: Root cause not yet isolated -- possibly polling-loop timing or self_pid exclusion edge case. Does not affect actual event delivery -- verified separately via pipeline hot_buffer counts (357->707 confirmed during a run that reported 0/0/0/0 stats).

title: Linux eBPF agent generates disproportionately high event volume vs Windows ETW agent
detail: Confirmed on cloud pipeline (July 11): Linux agent's 46 active probes flood the recent-events buffer, pushing Windows events out of default query windows within minutes. Not a data-loss bug -- Windows events remain retrievable via since_id=0 anchored search. Worth investigating whether all 46 Linux probes are capturing genuinely useful signal (e.g. sendmsg/gdbus noise) vs over-broad capture. Relevant for storage/query cost at scale with many customer endpoints.

title: C17 alert correlation confirmed working end-to-end after fixing 2 hardcoded-path bugs
detail: Following the earlier correlator import-path fix (relative to file location), a second hardcoded path was found in production: incidents.py had a fully literal path tied to one developer's username, and correlator.py had an unrelated second os.path.expanduser('~/ghostlayer/...') call not covered by the earlier fix. Both fixed via INCIDENTS_DB_PATH env var set to /data/ghostit_incidents.duckdb in Dockerfile.detection. Verified end-to-end with a real C14_LOLBIN_CHAIN alert (Explorer spawning PowerShell, confidence 85): log showed 'C17 incident updated: e07885d2', and direct DB query confirmed a correctly-populated incident record with proper MITRE ATT&CK mapping (Execution / T1059 Command and Scripting Interpreter), correct alert_count, and a readable summary. C17 is now confirmed functional, not just import-clean.

title: file_rename detection depends on an in-memory FileKey cache that resets on every agent restart -- explains why renames worked early in the session but stopped later
detail: Root cause identified (July 12, after ruling out scoring, fetch starvation, connection leak, and buffer-path bugs -- all real, all fixed, none were this specific issue): etw_provider.cpp file_key_cache_ only flags a rename as detected if the SAME FileKey was previously seen with a DIFFERENT name, within the CURRENT agent process's lifetime. The cache is purely in-memory, no persistence. Every service reinstall/restart (dozens happened this session) creates a fresh empty cache. When a test creates a file with New-Item then immediately renames it, if the agent restarted between or around those operations, the fresh cache sees the first NameCreate and just caches it as baseline (not flagged as rename) -- the actual rename is never detected because the cache never had the before state. Matches the observed pattern: early tests (finaltest, bigtest) worked with a warmed-up cache; later tests failed after multiple reinstalls for other fixes reset the cache each time. NOT a bug in the rename-detection logic itself -- it is an architectural fragility with no persistence across restarts. Real-world impact: only matters in the brief window right after an agent restart -- continuous sessions detect renames correctly, as proven by early clean runs. Fix options for later: (a) persist the FileKey cache to disk, (b) treat NameCreate as rename-relevant on first sight if extension matches known ransomware extensions (bypasses needing a cached before state), or (c) document as a narrow post-restart limitation similar to the ETW-TI/ELAM gap.

title: Firecracker honeypots require hardware virtualization (KVM) -- not available on budget cloud tiers or nested VMware setups
detail: Confirmed on AWS Lightsail Mumbai ($12/mo tier): 0 vmx/svm CPU flags, no /dev/kvm device -- Firecracker cannot run at all, not a config issue but a fundamental tier limitation. Also affects any nested-virtualization dev environment. Real architectural constraint: any customer's management server on similar budget/virtualized infrastructure would hit the same wall. Needs either (a) a KVM-capable instance tier for production deployments, or (b) an alternative honeypot sandboxing approach that doesn't require hardware virtualization (gVisor was previously rejected for timing-fingerprint reasons per Tech Spec 3.1).

title: Windows agent events never carried a baseline score, unlike Linux -- blocked C4 causal reasoning from seeing raw Windows telemetry (FIXED)
detail: Root cause: Linux Rust agent computes score=60/10 by priority for every event; Windows C9 agent sent no score field at all on raw file/process/network events. Server-side e.get('score') with no default returned None. Only detector-flagged alerts ever got a real score on Windows. Fixed: pipeline now assigns default priority-based scoring for any event arriving with score=None, matching Linux agent's own default. Verified with live data post-fix.

title: Detection engine capped at 500 events/10s poll cycle -- structurally starved by ~50k events/min Linux volume, causing Windows events to be crowded out (FIXED)
detail: Pipeline Parquet flush logs showed ~50,000 events/min Linux eBPF volume vs 500-event/10s (3000/min) detection engine fetch capacity. Fixed via per-host fetch quota in /events/since (split limit evenly across distinct hosts present), then extended with priority-tier fetch (file_rename/file_delete/process_exec/net_connect guaranteed bandwidth over file_write/file_open within each host's slice). Verified: event counts per fetch cycle dropped from hundreds to single digits/tens after fix.

title: Causal reasoning engine was never part of the Docker Compose stack -- never ran in the cloud deployment (FIXED)
detail: docker-compose.yml had no causal-engine service defined at all. C4 had been locally tested in prior sessions but never containerized/deployed. Added Dockerfile.causal (CPU-only PyTorch) and a causal-engine service entry. Also fixed two hardcoded ~/ghostlayer home-directory path bugs (module loader, provenance store DB path) that broke container startup, both made configurable via env vars. Verified: C4 now running continuously, confirmed via logs and live event processing.

title: C4 watchlist feedback loop built and functional, but full automatic end-to-end trigger from a real ransomware alert not cleanly isolated
detail: Built a pipeline-side watchlist (POST/GET /watchlist/{pid}) and wired C4's analyze_pid() to call it on invariant violation or high-confidence GNN classification -- closing the loop so C2 scoring gets more sensitive to confirmed-bad entities. Manually tested working (POST call correctly adds/expires PIDs). Full automatic trigger from a live Windows ransomware test was affected by several unrelated bugs found the same session (scoring gap, fetch starvation, connection leak, buffer path) -- by the time those were all fixed, session time was exhausted before a final clean end-to-end confirmation run.

title: file_rename events intermittently absent -- root cause found in RENAME-DETECTION-CACHE-FRAGILITY-01
detail: Extensive investigation (ruled out scoring, fetch starvation, connection leak, buffer-path bugs -- all real, all fixed, none were this specific issue) led to the actual root cause, documented separately in RENAME-DETECTION-CACHE-FRAGILITY-01: the in-memory FileKey rename-detection cache has no persistence across agent restarts. See that entry for full detail and fix options.

title: HTTP canary tokens confirmed working end-to-end via live-fire test
detail: Direct HTTP GET to a fake canary endpoint (/.env) on the deployed canary service (port 8080) immediately triggered two correctly-formed alerts: a raw canary_hit:http event (score 100) and a correlated R001 'Canary Token Triggered' detection with proper MITRE ATT&CK mapping (Discovery/T1056, confidence 100). Confirms the deception layer's simplest, most-used trap type (HTTP fake endpoints) works genuinely end-to-end in the live cloud deployment, not just as unverified code. Also separately confirmed working: PolymorphicTokenGenerator.create_token()/render() produces real, format-valid fake credentials (e.g. AKIA... AWS-format key). Note: two separate canary implementations exist in the codebase -- tokens.py/server.py (simpler, actively used, confirmed working here) and token_generator.py/token_validator.py (polymorphic, format-valid credential rendering, generation confirmed working but callback/validation flow not yet tested).

title: File canary tokens confirmed working end-to-end via live-fire test
detail: Reading a fake canary file (id_rsa, deployed at /var/lib/ghostit/canary/) triggered THREE separate correctly-labeled alerts capturing the full interaction lifecycle: file_open, file_read, and file_close_write, all score 100, all correctly identifying the specific decoy ('fake SSH private key'). Confirms C3's inotify-based FileCanaryWatcher works genuinely end-to-end in the live cloud deployment. Combined with CANARY-LIVE-FIRE-VERIFIED-01 (HTTP canaries), both of C3's file+HTTP deception trap types are now confirmed working with real evidence, not just present as code. Remaining untested C3 components: MTD (explicitly 0% per its own README, scaffolding only) and the separate PolymorphicTokenGenerator's callback/validation flow.

title: LKRG (kernel integrity monitoring) successfully built from source, loaded, and verified running -- V1.5 milestone
detail: Built lkrg.ko from official lkrg-org/lkrg GitHub source (matching kernel headers 7.0.0-27-generic already installed). Clean compile, loaded via insmod, confirmed active via lsmod and dmesg: 'LKRG initialized successfully', with kint_validate(1)/kint_enforce(2) and pint_validate(1)/pint_enforce(2) both active (kernel + process integrity validation and enforcement). Full tunable interface confirmed at /proc/sys/lkrg/ including pcfi_enforce/validate (Process Control-Flow Integrity -- functionally similar protective value to C18's intended ROP-chain detection, via a kernel-native mechanism that doesn't require hardware CPU tracing passthrough). Manually triggered a live integrity scan (echo 1 > trigger), confirmed real freeze/scan/restart cycle completes cleanly. This is real, running kernel-level protection, not scaffolding. Not yet done: wiring LKRG's dmesg/kernel-log output into the Ghost IT pipeline as structured events (currently just visible via dmesg, not yet forwarded as detection alerts).

title: MTD (Moving Target Deception) was code-complete but never included in Docker build -- fixed and core logic verified
detail: All three MTD files (rotator.py, topology_decoys.py, wireguard_announce.py) were internally marked STATUS: 100% complete, but the folder README incorrectly said 0%, and Dockerfile.canary never copied deception/mtd/ into the container at all. Fixed both (added COPY line, corrected README). Verified working: DeceptionAsset rotation scheduling (HMAC-jittered, correct due/not-due behavior confirmed with real timing tests) and TopologyDecoyManager initialization (real methods present: emit_arp_decoy, emit_mdns_decoy, flood_decoys, generate_decoys). wireguard_announce.py NOT yet tested -- requires a configured WireGuard interface (wg-ghostit) which does not exist on the current cloud deployment; needs separate infrastructure setup before live testing.

title: LKRG kernel events now flow into Ghost IT pipeline via lkrg_watcher.py -- V1.5 C19 fully functional end-to-end
detail: Built agent/lkrg_watcher.py: tails dmesg, classifies LKRG lines by concern level (kernel/process integrity violations, tainting, module verification failures = score 80; routine lifecycle = score 20), forwards as structured kernel_integrity events to the pipeline via the same TCP protocol used by C1/C9. Verified end-to-end: real LKRG boot events (including a genuine concerning event -- 'module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing') correctly landed in the pipeline with proper scoring, agent='lkrg-c19', type='kernel_integrity'. C19 is now a complete, working pipeline: kernel module (lkrg.ko) -> dmesg -> watcher -> pipeline -> (available to C2/C4/detection like any other event source). Not yet done: making lkrg_watcher.py a proper systemd service for persistent operation (currently run manually), and wiring specific LKRG violation types into dedicated detection rules rather than generic scoring.

title: SIEM export (CEF format) built and verified end-to-end -- V2 milestone
detail: Built integrations/siem/cef_formatter.py (converts Ghost IT alerts to valid CEF:0 format, correct severity mapping 0-10, proper field escaping) and siem_exporter.py (polls pipeline /alerts endpoint, forwards new alerts via UDP/TCP syslog to a configured SIEM host). Verified end-to-end with a real canary trigger: two genuine alerts (canary_hit + correlated R001 detection) correctly converted to valid CEF and received by a test UDP listener, with all fields properly populated (MITRE ATT&CK tactic/technique, severity, evidence, score). This is the actual feature format understood by Microsoft Sentinel, ArcSight, and many other SIEM platforms natively. Not yet done: LEEF format (QRadar) and Splunk CIM-compliant JSON export -- CEF chosen first for broadest single-format compatibility. Also not yet done: making siem_exporter.py a persistent systemd service, and adding TLS/authenticated syslog for production use (currently plain UDP/TCP, fine for demo/pilot but needs hardening before real customer deployment).
